Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the run chase. The umpires can be seen strolling out and so do the Nepal Under-19 fielders taking their respective field positions. Shamyl Hussain and Shahzaib Khan will open the batting for Pakistan Under-19 and it's Gulshan Jha with the new ball. Let's play...
...RUN CHASE...

Right then, Pakistan have a target within their reach and would aim to close the game by chasing it quickly to boost their net run rate. For Nepal, it will take nothing short of a miracle to turn the tide from here. An exciting run chase awaits us. Stay tuned.

Arafat Minhas is up for a quick chat for his excellent economical spell. He says that the pitch was supporting the spinners as it was dry and was spinning. Says that the fast bowling leaked away a bit more and the fielding too was not spot-on in patches. Closes by saying that he is very confident about the top 4 chasing it down.

As for Pakistan, Ahmad Hassan chipped in with a couple of scalps within the first powerplay and tried to build pressure right on. But the seamers bowled too many extras and gave easy singles to the opposition. They also shelled a catch which helped the Nepal batters stitch a good partnership. Though they didn't leak too many runs, they weren't able to provide the breakthrough till the 18th over. The spinners weaved a fantastic ploy and kept the batters tied up, giving them no room to cut loose and exerted the pressure at the right time. A couple of wickets of Bipin Rawal and Dev Khanal followed by a streak of maiden overs where Ali Asfand and Arafat Minhas dented their middle order as they kept bowling in tandem provided them the upper hand. Arafat Minhas ended up with brilliant figures with a 3-fer and he was economical as well. Pakistan restricted Nepal to a paltry 180 runs and the spinners pulled things to their favour dominating the middle over phase. Ubaid Shah with a couple of caught and bowleds picked a couple as well.

This brings us to the end of the first half of play and Nepal Under-19, after a sluggish first inning, have posted something to defend here. Nepal U-19 lost two early wickets in the form of Arjun Kumal and Aakash Tripathi but the skipper Dev Khanal and Bipin Rawal faired well and steered their ship steadily by stitching up a resilient partnership of 37 runs. They both were pretty watchful with the shots and smartly avoided unnecessary shots and kept rotating strike. But the runs literally dried up after Khanal's departure as they consumed too many dot deliveries with no real intent to take on the spinners. The middle order tumbled badly after Bipin Rawal perished on a sluggish 33. The scoring manhattan flattened up in the middle overs and no batter barring the former two looked comfortable and the pressure kept piling up. Subhash Bhandari and Aakash Chand showed some attacking intent at the backend and constructed a 25-run partnership and helped them to post 197. Nepal managed to hit only 11 boundaries and 3 sixes throughout innings.
